reason: E4 supports that lattice distortion reduces phonon velocity and thermal conductivity. E2 supports the use of Debye temperature as a descriptor correlated with thermal conductivity. E1 provides experimental thermal conductivity data but does not address predictive modeling. No cited evidence supports the claimed ±10% prediction accuracy, the specific descriptors (force-constant fluctuations, group velocities) as model inputs, or the >50% error of conventional approaches. E3 shows force-constant fluctuations are not necessarily enhanced in HEAs, partially conflicting with the mechanism premise.
premises: Lattice distortion in HEAs reduces phonon group velocity and enhances phonon scattering, leading to low lattice thermal conductivity.
Descriptors such as force-constant fluctuations, Debye temperature, and acoustic phonon group velocities can quantitatively capture these effects.
An integrated DFT-ML model using these descriptors can predict lattice thermal conductivity within ±10% of experimental values.
Conventional cocktail or ideal solution approaches deviate by over 50% from experimental values.
